title: Tailr Core connector
description: connector.json of a Tailr Core connector (or a single connector JSON file). See docs/koppelingen-maken.md.

$schema.description: The JSON schema of this file, for completion in your editor.

baseUrl.description: Base URL of the API, e.g. https://api.mollie.com/v2. May contain {{VARS}}.

auth.description: How Tailr Core signs in at the source: oauth2, bearer, basic, header, query or none.

tools.description: The functions: each one is one call.

$schema.description: The JSON schema of this file, for completion in your editor.

The JSON schema of this file, for completion in your editor.

intro.description: Short explanation shown on the user's overview. Plain text, no HTML.

whatsNew.description: Short explanation shown with a newly available module. Plain text; not a separate event per function.

adminOnly.description: Only show this content to administrators. Useful for administration plugins.

title.description: Short, task-focused title for the question, e.g. Which orders need attention? The full prompt is copied unchanged.

prompt.description: A useful question the user can copy to their AI tool. Use plain language, not function names.

requires.description: Function names needed for this example. Connector: local function names; plugin: qualified function names. Only shown if the user may use all of them through AI.

__schema12.description: Unique id: lower-case letters, digits, - and _ (at most 48).

__schema14.description: Name of the system, e.g. Mollie.

__schema15.description: Version (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH). Raise it on every change.

__schema23.description: Release maturity, shown separately from the description.

__schema27.description: Id of the main connector this one is a variant of (same system, another way to sign in). A variant is not listed separately under Available; it is offered on the connect page of the main connector.

__schema28.description: Short name of this route, e.g. "Sign in with your own Google account". English source, with optional translations.

__schema29.description: Settings the administrator fills in (keys, URLs). Use them as {{NAME}}.

name.description: Name in UPPER_CASE, used as {{NAME}} in baseUrl, auth, headers and defaults.

label.description: Label on the setup page. English source, with optional translations.

description.description: Where the administrator finds this value at the source.

secret.description: Secret values are encrypted and never shown again (default true). Use false for e.g. a shop URL.

multiline.description: Multi-line value, e.g. the JSON key file of a service account. The setup page shows a text area to paste it in.

__schema35.description: Extra hosts this connector may reach besides the host of baseUrl or url; the login only goes to these hosts.

__schema38.description: Code functions (tools/*.ts in the folder). They always run in the sandbox.

__schema47.description: The result after transforms, before privacy protection. A self-contained JSON Schema 2020-12; invalid results are withheld. For privacy-marked tools Core omits this schema from the AI-facing definition because fields may be hidden or pseudonymized.

__schema53.description: File in the connector folder, e.g. tools/settlement_breakdown.ts. Give file or code.

__schema56.description: Functions the code may call with ctx.call: a function of this connector ("list_items") or alias.function for a connection from requires.

__schema59.description: Requests the code may make with ctx.request: method plus path relative to baseUrl (* = one segment, ** = the rest).

__schema67.description: For the AI: what to fill in, with the format.

__schema75.description: Who may call this function: "all" (the AI and the API, default) or "api" (only dashboards, tools and apps; never the AI over MCP). Use "api" when the data may go to a dashboard or tool but not into the chat. The connector sets the minimum: an administrator can make a function API-only, never undo it. See docs/koppelingen-maken.md, "Privacygevoelige velden en functies".

__schema77.description: Mark a function that returns data about people (names, email, phone, address, bank account, salary, health). Tailr Core then lets only the fields in sensitivity pass, gives the AI pseudonyms by default, works one person at a time (lookup required, at most maxRecords), applies a daily limit per user, never caches it, and logs every lookup. The connector sets the minimum: an administrator can only make it stricter. See docs/koppelingen-maken.md, "Privacygevoelige velden en functies".

__schema78.description: Per field of a record: "none", "personal" (name, email, address), "financial" (IBAN, salary) or "special" (health, citizen service number). Only these fields pass (allowlist); fields that are not "none" get a pseudonym for the AI.

__schema81.description: Field with the id of the person in each record (default id).

__schema83.description: Parameters to look up one person (id, number or email). At least one is required on every call; a list without a filter is refused.

__schema85.description: Where the records are in the response, e.g. items. Default: the response itself.

__schema87.description: At most this many records per call (default 1).

__schema89.description: At most this many different people per user per day (default 100).

__schema91.description: Word for the pseudonym, e.g. "Customer" gives "Customer #K7Q2MX".

allowReal.description: Sensitive scalar fields eligible for explicit disclosure to an AI client. Omitted fields stay pseudonymized. Core applies its own allow/ask/deny policy; this is not consent.

__schema98.description: Improvements to the standard setup guide: steps at the source, testWith, prerequisites.

loginNote.description: Tip at the step where the admin signs in at the source, e.g. a warning the source shows.

flow.description: authorization_code: the administrator signs in. client_credentials: Tailr Core fetches a token with client id and secret. jwt_bearer: Tailr Core signs a JWT with the key of a service account (no sign-in step).

assertion.description: Only with flow jwt_bearer: how the JWT assertion is built (fromJsonKey for a Google service account, or issuer and privateKey).

__schema108.description: Setting with the JSON key file of a service account (Google), e.g. {{SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY}}. The issuer and private key are read from it.

__schema110.description: The iss claim. With fromJsonKey it defaults to client_email from the key file.

__schema112.description: Optional sub claim, e.g. the user the service account acts for.

__schema114.description: The aud claim; defaults to tokenUrl.

__schema116.description: Private key in PEM. With fromJsonKey it defaults to private_key from the key file.

name.description: Function name: letters, digits and _. The AI sees <connection>__<name>.

description.description: For the AI: what the function returns, when to use it, and the shape of the parameters.

confirmationRequired.description: Require confirmation of every exact invocation. An administrator cannot turn this requirement off.

level.description: read = only looks; write = creates or changes; admin = deletes, money or sending.

path.description: Path after baseUrl, with {param} for path parameters.

params.description: Parameters the AI fills in, by name.

transform.description: Leave out (exclude) or pick (select) fields before the answer goes to the AI.

in.description: Where the parameter goes: path ({name} in path), query, body or header.
